patterns: James Talarico was the weekend's biggest story by far: 30 hits and ~6.9M views, led by two Gunther posts at ~3.1M (his 96.8% party-line Texas House record) and ~3.05M (Daily Wire hidden camera on his transgender policies). Like rates were tiny (0.1% and 0.6%), so these spread on reach and shares, not agreement

Election-integrity framing was everywhere: 87 hits (~7.4M views) mention voting, ballots, polls, cheating or fraud, from Brazil's Supreme Court extending voting hours (~182k, follow-up 'I called it' ~93k at 6.9%) to Tarrant County early-vote warnings (~78k) and Maine translators at polling stations (~64k)
Ilhan Omar stayed hot: 19 hits, ~1.29M views. Trump declaring her seat forfeited (~378k at 8.0%) and the short 'Expel and remove Ilhan Omar' note to Speaker Johnson (~84k at 18.0%) did best

Foreign unrest and foreign elections travel well: France, Paris, Barcelona and Finland posts drew 20 hits and ~1.53M (Finland elderly man harassed ~622k at 3.4%), and Conservatives winning British Columbia hit ~154k at 11.0%

Michigan stayed a main battleground: 40 hits, ~2.0M views, covering El-Sayed's Bret Baier interview, Obama's Michigan rally (mocking Hegseth ~188k at 10.7%), and a Dearborn mom's warning (~86k at 13.8%)

Short one-line verdicts again had the best like rates: Elon on Charlie Kirk (20.9%), 'stop the cheat in California' (18.4%), expel Omar (18.0%), Liberty University worship (16.2%), 'France can happen here' (16.2%), Thune and the SAVE America Act (14.8% on ~147k)
Ask-@Grok posts kept pulling reach but not loyalty: 16 of them drew ~1.77M (Fermi paradox ~442k, worst news network ~385k, 2026 fraud-risk states ~274k) at 0.2-0.7% likes

rawsalerts won on odd consumer and history headlines rather than politics: Airbnb hosts threatening to sue over guest-chore rules (~838k), Hitler's Eagle's Nest fire (~483k), and Polymarket affiliates complaining about payouts (~178k); alx's top post was Bernie Sanders and the $1 million Michigan donation (~511k)
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, 50 posts) leaned hard into AI and money fear. The biggest was @WatcherGuru (~1.25M) relaying Elon Musk's warning that lenders have almost cut off funding to companies that live off AI data center revenue, followed by 'digital and banking lockdown' threads from @SternDrewCrypto (~689k) and @MarioNawfal (~248k). The most newsworthy item was a Washington Post exclusive from @lizzadwoskin (~211k) saying ex-DOGE cyber researchers used AI agents to get into Anthropic's systems, including internal Slack channels, in under 12 hours; @Polymarket repeated it (~80k). Other threads were CZ saying AI agents will pay with crypto instead of cards (@coinbureau ~167k), @Noahpinion on 'swarms of rogue AI agents' (~97k), and Google clearing ~250,000 trees in Finland for a data center (@allenanalysis ~25k). The rest was mostly free-course spam and tiny accounts, since X's search again ignored the likes filter.
narrative_synthesis: The weekend was the biggest window on record for the watchlist: 524 hits and ~31.5M views, with Gunther's two Talarico posts alone taking ~6.1M at very low like rates. Underneath that, the base ran on election-integrity framing at home and abroad, Ilhan Omar's seat, and short verdict lines that keep getting the best like rates. Open angles: judge Talarico by his record instead of his ads, election rules that change on election day, the AI-agent hacking story as a reason to be careful what you paste into chatbots, and a one-line push on the SAVE America Act eight days out.
